relevance_note: The paper reports two identifiable SSADH-deficiency patients in individual detail ('We evaluated VEPs on two patients with confirmed SSADH deficiency.'), including patient 1's homozygous variant 'c.667T>C' and his two carrier parents.
method_note: Worked by hand from the paper, schema and rules; no script was used and the paper contains no tables, so nothing had to be transcribed from a table and no stacked-cell columns exist. In scope: patient 1, patient 2 (both with SSADH deficiency) and the two parents of patient 1, who were tested and found heterozygous ('T/C heterozygotes at position c.667'). The mother mentioned once in the VEP methodology ('his mother’s lap') is assumed to be one of those two tested parents, so no third relative row was created. Patient 2's variant is not printed anywhere in the paper (only 'molecular confirmation of the diagnosis was previously achieved in white cells'), so her variants row is kept with variant_original_string 'not reported' and no gene symbol, as nothing is printed for her. SNP rs2744583 was not recorded as a variant row: the authors use it only as a marker ('providing further evidence that they carried two copies of the SSADH gene not deleted in exon 4'), not as a causal variant. Because both parents carry c.667T>C, patient 1's homozygous variant is inherited from both parents; the schema has no 'both parents' value, so 'inherited unspecified parent' was used. The missense class was recorded for the parents' variant because the paper says the missense mutation's homozygous state 'was confirmed by sequencing genomic DNA from his parents, who were T/C heterozygotes at position c.667'; pathogenicity and functional evidence were left 'not reported' for the parents because those statements are about the proband's nucleotide alteration. Patient 2's hyperkinesis was not mapped to the checklist item 'attention problems or ADHD'. Her current age is not stated (only 'after a 20-year follow-up'), so age_at_last_evaluation was taken from the age at which her VEPs were recorded ('age 9 years'). No contradicting statements were found in the paper.
